- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.36) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (especially if sentiment drops post-spike) — adjust downward bias.
- Overshoot in early forecast horizon (e.g., 30d) when sentiment is rising — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 18-day moving average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment confirms trend.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment peaks 2–3 days before forecast horizon, model should adjust downward to reflect delayed reaction.
- Avoid overconfidence in high sentiment + high recent price — reduce forecast volatility if sentiment >0.44 and price >80.00.
- Correct for “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is high but price is flat, forecast should not rise unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive days of rising price.
